name: Minimum Projected Teaching-Set Size / Projected Minimum Degree
details: For every finite binary class, the minimum projected teaching-set size dominates projected minimum degree.
proof: For each coordinate projection, every target's teaching-set size is at least its degree in the projected $1$-inclusion graph. Therefore $\min_h\max_T\operatorname{ts}(h,\mathcal H_{|T})\ge\max_T\min_h\operatorname{ts}(h,\mathcal H_{|T})\ge\max_T\mathrm d_{\min}(\mathcal H_{|T})=\mathrm d^p_{\min}(\mathcal H)$.
proof_source: Corollary \ref{cor:projected-min-teaching-degree} in the survey, using Lemma \ref{lem:teaching-set-degree-lower-bound}.
witness_verification: For the family #classes/singletons with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $n-1$ and $1$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity as n tends to infinity, ruling out every reverse affine-linear bound. See the database-owned value proofs for these two endpoints.
